hq_country: United Kingdom (Sage HQ Newcastle, UK; Inventory Planner originally founded with US operations)
target_segment: SMB to mid-market e-commerce brands (typically $1M+ annual revenue)
target_vertical: Multi-channel retailer / DTC brand / wholesaler — primarily Shopify and Amazon-based e-commerce brands plus wholesale/B2B
pricing_model: Custom revenue-based tiered pricing (scales with annual GMV/revenue and number of connected channels/SKUs). Quote-based — no public per-user pricing. Typically annual contract.
starting_price_usd: ~$244.99/month entry tier (widely reported floor; some sources cite from $100/month for very small accounts) [uncertain]
free_trial_or_freemium: 14-day free trial available; book-a-demo flow on website; Shopify App Store listing offers free install with trial
shopify_install_count: ~146 reviews on Shopify App Store; vendor claims 2,600+ brands across platforms [uncertain]
shopify_built_for_shopify_badge: No (not listed as Built for Shopify certified as of May 2026) [uncertain]
shopify_plus_partner_status: Yes — listed/positioned as a Shopify Plus partner integration (Shopify Plus is explicitly named in vendor integration docs) [uncertain]
shopify_sync_direction: Primarily one-way read from Shopify (sales history, products, inventory levels, POs/receipts). Inventory Planner is described as 'mostly a read-only service' that does not create/edit/remove products or sales orders. Purchase order received-quantities can optionally write back stock updates to the storefront in some integrations.
shopify_synced_entities: Products, variants, inventory levels (by location), orders/sales history, purchase orders/receipts, vendor and supplier metadata, multi-location stock. Customers and fulfillments are not primary sync targets — Inventory Planner is a forecasting/replenishment layer, not an OMS.
shopify_service_item_support: Not a documented focus — product is forecasting-driven and typically ignores or filters service/non-stock items. No public marketing of service-item sync parity. [uncertain]
shopify_multi_store_support: Yes — multiple Shopify stores can be connected to a single Inventory Planner account; multi-store aggregation is a documented use case.
shopify_pos_support: Shopify POS sales are ingested via Shopify order history (POS orders flow through standard Shopify channels). No dedicated POS-specific UI. [uncertain]
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: No specific documentation of native Shopify B2B (Plus) catalogs / company locations / price lists handling. [uncertain]
shopify_markets_support: No specific documentation of Shopify Markets multi-market pricing / duties / landed cost awareness. [uncertain]
shopify_metafield_to_erp_field_mapping: Not a documented feature — Inventory Planner exposes its own custom fields and tags but does not market a generic metafield <-> custom-field mapping equivalent to Brightpearl's. [uncertain]
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants/SKUs are imported 1:1 from Shopify and used as the planning unit. Variant options are preserved; bundles are handled via Inventory Planner's own assemblies/kits logic.
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Scheduled / batched sync (typically every few hours; some data points refreshed daily). Not a real-time webhook-driven sync — forecasts and replenishment are recalculated on a periodic basis. [uncertain]
shopify_known_limitations: Read-mostly integration so it cannot push catalog/listing edits. Periodic (not real-time) sync means inventory and sales reflect with lag. Long recalculation/loading times reported for large catalogs. Seasonal SKU forecasting can be inconsistent with limited history. Onboarding typically ~4 weeks. 12-month auto-renewing contract is a frequent complaint.
etsy_native_or_third_party: Listed as a directly supported sales channel in Inventory Planner's marketplace integrations list. Native connector. [uncertain]
etsy_listing_creation_vs_sync_only: Sync only — Inventory Planner does not create or manage Etsy listings; it ingests sales and inventory for forecasting.
etsy_inventory_sync: Read-only ingest of Etsy sales history and current inventory levels for forecasting. Frequency is the standard scheduled sync (hours to daily). [uncertain]
etsy_order_import: Etsy orders/sales imported on the scheduled sync cadence; used as demand signal, not for fulfillment workflows. [uncertain]
etsy_synced_entities: Listings (as products), variations, inventory levels, orders/receipts (for sales history). No shipping/fulfillment write-back. [uncertain]
etsy_known_limitations: Forecasting-only role; cannot create or edit Etsy listings, personalization fields, or digital products. Variation-level granularity depends on how the Etsy account is structured. [uncertain]
amazon_marketplaces: Global Amazon Seller Central marketplaces supported via SP-API (US, CA, MX, UK, EU marketplaces, AU, JP). Exact marketplace matrix not enumerated publicly. [uncertain]
amazon_seller_types: FBA and FBM supported (Amazon Seller Central). Vendor Central (1P) is not a documented native integration. [uncertain]
amazon_synced_entities: Listings/products, inventory levels (including FBA on-hand, inbound, reserved), orders/sales history, basic settlement/returns data is read in for demand signal. Forecasts and PO recommendations are produced from this; Inventory Planner does not push listings or labels back to Amazon. [uncertain]
amazon_listing_creation: Sync only — no listing creation/edits pushed back to Amazon Seller Central.
amazon_repricing_support: None — repricing is out of scope; Inventory Planner is a forecasting/replenishment tool, not a repricer.
amazon_buy_shipping: Not supported — no in-app Amazon Buy Shipping label purchase.
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: Inventory Planner generates FBA replenishment recommendations and can create FBA inbound shipment plans / POs that feed Seller Central; the actual inbound creation flow leverages SP-API. Whether the new Fulfillment Inbound v2024-03-20 API is fully adopted is not publicly confirmed. [uncertain]
amazon_sp_api_inbound_v2024_03_20: Migration status to v2024-03-20 inbound API not publicly documented. [uncertain]
amazon_settlement_report_handling: Not an accounting tool — settlement reports are not posted to a ledger. Settlement/financial data flow (if any) is via the connected accounting system (QBO/Xero) or downstream tooling. [uncertain]
amazon_marketplace_facilitator_tax_handl: Not handled — marketplace tax journaling is the accounting system's responsibility. [uncertain]
amazon_multi_account_support: Multiple Amazon Seller Central accounts can be connected to a single Inventory Planner tenant. [uncertain]
amazon_known_limitations: Forecasting-only role: no listing edits, no repricing, no Buy Shipping, no settlement posting. Sync is periodic rather than real-time. Vendor Central (1P) not natively supported.
xero_app_store_certified: Listed on the Xero App Store / marketplace. No public award/badge listing such as Global App Award beyond standard certification. [uncertain]
xero_app_awards_recognition: Not a documented Xero Global App Award finalist as of May 2026. [uncertain]
xero_app_store_rating: Not publicly highlighted; Xero App Store listing rating/review count not stated in available sources. [uncertain]
xero_synced_entities: Purchase orders pushed from Inventory Planner to Xero. Supplier (contact) data referenced for POs. Xero is treated as a complementary connector — primary inventory/sales source comes from Shopify/Amazon/WooCommerce/etc. Invoices, payments, COGS journals are not the focus.
xero_accounting_sync_mode: Not an invoice-per-order or summary-journal accounting connector — Xero integration is limited to purchase-order push (procurement workflow), not sales-side bookkeeping.
xero_cogs_journal_method: Not applicable — Inventory Planner does not post COGS journals to Xero.
xero_multi_currency: Xero multi-currency invoices/bills are supported by Xero itself; Inventory Planner-pushed POs respect supplier currency where Xero supports it. [uncertain]
xero_tax_handling: Tax codes on pushed POs map to Xero supplier defaults; no advanced tax engine. [uncertain]
xero_known_limitations: Xero is described as a complementary connector — cannot supply primary inventory or sales history on its own. PO push only; no sales invoice or COGS posting back to Xero.
qb_desktop_supported: Yes — QuickBooks Desktop is supported via the QuickBooks Desktop API connection (separate setup from QBO).
qb_app_certified: Listed on the Intuit App Store (QuickBooks App Store listing exists for Inventory Planner by Sage). [uncertain]
qb_app_store_rating: Intuit App Store rating/review count not stated in available sources. [uncertain]
qb_synced_entities: Products, sales/invoices (as demand history), purchase orders, suppliers/vendors. QuickBooks can act as the primary source of sales/inventory data when Shopify/Amazon are not present. Inventory Planner reads sales and inventory; it can push purchase orders back to QuickBooks.
qb_accounting_sync_mode: Not an invoice-per-order accounting integration — Inventory Planner reads sales/inventory from QuickBooks to drive forecasts, and pushes POs/replenishment. Not a sales-journal poster.
qb_cogs_journal_method: Not applicable — Inventory Planner does not post COGS journals to QuickBooks. COGS valuation lives in QuickBooks's own inventory module.
qb_multi_currency: QuickBooks Online multi-currency is supported by QBO itself; Inventory Planner respects supplier currency on POs where QBO supports it. [uncertain]
qb_known_limitations: QB connector is for forecasting and PO push, not for accounting automation. Real-time push is limited — periodic sync only. QuickBooks Desktop API path requires the desktop installation to be reachable for sync.
other_ecom_channels: WooCommerce (native), BigCommerce (native), eBay (native), Etsy (native), Walmart (native), Square (native), Lightspeed (native), Magento (via partner/ERP layer), Cin7 (native), Linnworks (native), Brightpearl (native via sibling Sage product), Ongoing WMS (native), ShipHero (native), ShipBob (native), NetSuite (native), Microsoft Dynamics 365 (native), Unleashed (partner integration).
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Yes — Inventory Planner supports assemblies/kits/bundles; component stock is decremented when a bundle sells and bundle availability is computed from components. [uncertain]
other_accounting_integrations: QuickBooks Online and Desktop (native), Xero (native), NetSuite (native via ERP connector), Microsoft Dynamics 365 (native). Sage Intacct via the Sage ecosystem. Direct Sage 50 / MYOB / FreshBooks / Wave / Zoho Books integrations are not documented as native. [uncertain]
bom_support: Limited — supports kits/assemblies/bundles for finished-goods composition, but not a full manufacturing BOM engine like Katana/Cin7. [uncertain]
multi_level_bom: Not supported as a manufacturing feature — Inventory Planner is not positioned as a manufacturing/MRP tool. [uncertain]
production_orders: Not supported — no work orders / production orders / routings. Manufacturing workflows are handled by partner ERPs (Brightpearl, NetSuite, Cin7, Dynamics 365).
batch_lot_tracking: Not a documented native feature; relies on connected source system. [uncertain]
serial_tracking: Not a documented native feature; relies on connected source system. [uncertain]
bin_location_support: Not a native feature — Inventory Planner plans at the warehouse/location level, not bin/aisle. Bin-level data lives in the WMS/ERP. [uncertain]
multi_warehouse: Yes — multi-warehouse / multi-location planning is a core strength. Supports per-location forecasts, stock balancing, and warehouse transfer recommendations.
barcoding: Not a documented native feature — barcoding/label printing handled by the WMS/3PL. [uncertain]
purchase_orders: Yes — purchase order creation, partial receipts, supplier price lists, vendor lead times, MOQs, and auto-generated POs from replenishment recommendations are core features. POs can be pushed to connected accounting / ERP / WMS systems.
supplier_management: Yes — supplier records, lead times, MOQs, supplier-SKU mapping, multiple suppliers per SKU, preferred supplier rules, and cost tracking.
landed_cost_support: Supports cost-of-goods inputs including freight/duty allocations for forecasting and PO valuation purposes. Not a full landed-cost accounting engine. [uncertain]
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: Supplier costs and PO totals can be tracked in supplier currency; inventory valuation typically resolves to base currency. [uncertain]
ai_demand_forecasting: Yes — demand forecasting is the core product. Multiple forecasting models (retail, wholesale, seasonal, non-seasonal) factor in seasonality, trends, marketing events, and lead times. Marketed as statistical/data-driven forecasting; AI/ML branding has increased post-Sage. [uncertain]
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Yes — automated replenishment and PO draft suggestions are core. Determines when and how much to reorder per supplier, with one-click PO creation.
ai_natural_language_query: Not a documented feature as of May 2026. [uncertain]
public_api: Public API exists via the Sage Developer Portal (developer.sage.com/inventory-planner). REST-based. API quality and breadth are not as widely documented as Shopify's. [uncertain]
webhook_event_coverage: Webhook support exists within the Sage developer ecosystem; specific Inventory Planner event coverage is not extensively documented publicly. [uncertain]
integration_architecture: Native — direct connectors built and maintained by Inventory Planner/Sage to each platform (Shopify, Amazon, QBO, Xero, WooCommerce, etc.).
zapier_make_support: No official Zapier/Make/n8n connector documented as of May 2026. Third-party connectors (e.g. APIWORX) exist for custom integration. [uncertain]
mobile_app: No dedicated native mobile app — the product is a web-based application optimized for desktop planning workflows. [uncertain]
mobile_barcode_scanning_app: No — barcode scanning is not in scope for a forecasting/planning tool.
rate_limit_handling_documented: Rate-limit handling for Shopify/Amazon/Xero/QBO is not publicly detailed in customer-facing documentation. [uncertain]
sync_frequency: Periodic / batched. Typically multiple syncs per day (every few hours) across Shopify, Amazon, WooCommerce, QBO/Xero. Not webhook-driven real-time. [uncertain]
shipping_carrier_integrations: None directly — shipping carriers are handled by connected ShipStation, ShipBob, ShipHero, Ongoing WMS, etc. ShipStation has a documented partner page with Inventory Planner.
shipping_label_buying: No — labels are not purchased inside Inventory Planner.
three_pl_integrations: Yes — ShipBob (native), ShipHero (native), Ongoing WMS (native), and via partner ERPs (Brightpearl, NetSuite, Cin7). FBA inventory is treated as a 3PL-like channel via Amazon SP-API.
edi_support: Not a native feature — EDI typically handled by the connected ERP or 3PL. [uncertain]
g2_rating: ~4.6 / 5 on G2 based on weighted distribution of recent reviews (71% five-star, 26% four-star). Specific review count not pinned but small (<100 reviews). [uncertain]
g2_grid_quadrant: Listed in G2's Demand Planning / Inventory Control categories; specific 2026 Grid quadrant placement (Leader / High Performer / Niche) not confirmed in available sources. [uncertain]
capterra_rating: Capterra rating ~4.2 / 5 with ~ low-hundreds reviews on the Inventory Planner profile. (4.2 with ~1,944 reviews figure cited by one source appears to be a Capterra-wide aggregate, not Inventory Planner-specific.) [uncertain]
notable_customers: Vendor claims 2,600+ brands. Public customer names include high-growth Shopify/Shopify Plus DTC brands and multi-channel retailers; specific named case studies are featured on the inventory-planner.com site but not enumerated here. [uncertain]
last_major_release: Inventory Planner releases new capabilities multiple times a year; specific most-recent release name/date not publicly summarized in a changelog as of May 2026. Recent direction (post-Sage acquisition) has emphasized Sage ecosystem alignment, improved forecasting models, and tighter Brightpearl interop. [uncertain]
owner_parent_company: Sage Group plc — Sage acquired Brightpearl in January 2022; Brightpearl had acquired Inventory Planner in September 2021. Product was renamed to 'Inventory Planner by Sage' in June 2022.
last_funding_event: Acquired by Brightpearl September 2021 (~$10M reported, 70% cash / 30% equity). Brightpearl (with Inventory Planner) acquired by Sage in January 2022 (Sage took the remaining 83% of Brightpearl it did not already own, deal estimated around $360M for Brightpearl).
public_status_page_uptime: Sage operates status pages across its products; Inventory Planner SLA terms are published at inventory-planner.com/customer-terms/sla/. A dedicated public status-page URL with live uptime is not prominently published. [uncertain]
